recommendations.description: Launch a Yale New Haven Hospital CT Commercial Individual PPO acute inpatient audit for authorization-required admissions to confirm prior authorization, denial enforcement, auth-to-claim matching, level-of-care and discharge management, and claims processing per contractual obligation for craniotomy and sepsis episodes, with site-of-care or contract remediation review for persistent outlier costs.
evidence: Increase concentrated at YALE NEW HAVEN HOSPITAL.
Authorization-required CT PPO acute hospital admissions drove the pattern.

United Health shows no inpatient DRG scope; only microsurgery reimbursement limits.

recommendations.description: Implement a KY IP Med/Surg inpatient claims and contract compliance review, starting with NORTON HOSPITAL, across ACUTE HOSPITAL HMO PA=Y, ACUTE HOSPITAL PPO PA=N, and CHILDRENS HMO PA=Y to verify prior authorization match status, enforce denied-authorization adjudication edits, review utilization management KPI changes, and confirm contract-compliant reimbursement for flagged service subsets including Uterine and Adnexa Procedures for Nonmalignancy without CC/MCC.

KY PPO acute hospitals added about +$1.5M despite 20 fewer admissions.

KY childrens HMO added about +$1.2M on 6 more admissions.
Source cards flag auth-to-claim validation and repeated delta concentration.
Impacted DRG includes Uterine and Adnexa Procedures for Nonmalignancy without CC/MCC.

recommendations.description: Launch a claims policy audit to reconcile PA-required AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION logic and Not Mapped facility assignments across ME, CA, GA, TX, KY, CT, and VA, and reprocess affected claims for MaineHealth Maine Medical Center Portland, Santa Clara Valley Medical Center, Parkland Health and Hospital System, and Norton Hospital, prioritizing Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC, Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC, and Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours without MCC.

ME AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION shows about -$2.5M redistribution.
CA craniotomy at Santa Clara Valley Medical Center moved about +$1.7M.
KY, CT, and VA contain additional spend in Not Mapped facilities.

recommendations.description: Implement a cross-market Commercial Individual HMO and POS acute-hospital policy review for MEMORIAL HOSPITAL and ELKHART GENERAL HOSPITAL to audit authorization-denial enforcement and claims processing, and pursue contract or site-of-care remediation with itemized bill review for recurrent Craniotomy and Endovascular Intracranial Procedures with MCC, Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours without MCC, and Aftercare, Musculoskeletal System and Connective Tissue with CC admissions.
evidence: Recurring acute-hospital groups sum to about +$6.1M.
MEMORIAL HOSPITAL added about +$838K in Indiana HMO acute-hospital admissions.
ELKHART GENERAL HOSPITAL added about +$541K across Indiana HMO and POS findings.
Craniotomy with MCC added about +$2.7M across Georgia and Colorado HMO markets.
Texas and Nevada sepsis episodes added about +$627K.
Auth-required source cards are flagged for auth-to-claim validation.

recommendations.description: Initiate a focused TX IP Med/Surg sepsis UM audit at PARKLAND HEALTH AND HOSPITAL SYSTEM for DRG "Septicemia or Severe Sepsis without Mechanical Ventilation >96 Hours without MCC," prioritizing SEPSIS UNSPECIFIED ORGANISM, SEPSIS D/O ESCHERICHIA COLI E COLI, SEPSIS D/T METHICILLIN RSIST STAPH, and BACTEREMIA to verify admission criteria, acute level-of-care decisions, initial and concurrent review performance, and prior-authorization-to-claim matching.
evidence: TX sepsis-related clinical groups total about +$1.8M.
Unspecified sepsis added about +$1.1M on 94 more admissions.
E. coli sepsis added about +$299K on 18 more admissions.
MRSA sepsis and bacteremia added about +$409K with higher per-admit intensity.
All cited cases show PA-required code Y and ER admit indicator Y.
Provider context shows PARKLAND HEALTH AND HOSPITAL SYSTEM in TX.
peer_benchmarking: BCBS_TX reviews sepsis DRGs for diagnosis accuracy and requires infection, organ dysfunction, and sequencing support.
Molina may adjust payment after pre/post-payment DRG clinical validation when Sepsis-3 support is insufficient.
Parkland Community Health Plan clinically validates sepsis DRGs pre- and post-payment using Sepsis-3 and SOFA documentation.

IP MedSurg (DNE) Trend 3: The variance is highly concentrated in a narrow set of rare, high-cost neuro and orthopedic diagnoses such as craniotomy with traumatic subdural hematoma, cerebral aneurysm, degenerative neurologic disorders, and orthopedic aftercare, making diagnosis-level isolation the strongest parent rule.; IP MedSurg (DNE) Trend 4: The pattern spans multiple care settings tied to the same episode types—acute hospital, long term care hospital, physical rehab, and NF—so service/site-of-care concentration is a core driver to evaluate.; IP MedSurg (DNE) Trend 7: The recommended next step explicitly calls for discharge pathway review, and the pattern shows inpatient neuro/orthopedic episodes flowing into post-acute settings, making admission/discharge source and location highly relevant.; IP MedSurg (DNE) Trend 8: The main operational cards are all authorization-related (pa_required_code = Y) and flagged for auth-to-claim validation, so confirming whether authorization controls were enforced is directly relevant.; IP MedSurg (DNE) Trend 10: Paid per admit increased materially and the pattern calls for payment-term and reimbursement review, so reimbursement method is a key parent rule for explaining the high-cost EPO acute and post-acute episode spend.
